rules.statement: Parse date/time strings through `NCode.Json.DateCoercion.TryParseDateTimeOffset` or `TryParseDateTime` instead of calling `DateTime.TryParse`/`DateTimeOffset.TryParse` directly.
rules.why: Hand-rolled parsing duplicates the shared date coercion policy and drifts from it, so different packages end up accepting different formats or producing different values.
rules.check: Look for new `DateTime.TryParse`, `DateTimeOffset.TryParse`, `DateTime.Parse` or `DateTimeOffset.Parse` calls on date strings in production code where `DateCoercion` should be used.

rules.statement: Do not fall back to `DateTime` parsing when a `DateTimeOffset` parse fails, because the fallback silently clamps an out-of-range instant to a machine-local value instead of failing.
rules.why: The fallback only runs when the instant can't be represented, and then it produces a wrong instant instead of a failure.
rules.check: Look for code that tries `DateTimeOffset` parsing and then, if that fails, parses the same text as `DateTime`.

rules.statement: When decoding JSON into claims or other loosely-typed values, keep a JSON string as a plain string with its exact value, and never infer a date (or any other type) from what the string looks like.
rules.why: Lenient sniffing changes signed data after verification ("1.2" becomes a date, "10:30" becomes today, an OIDC `birthdate` loses its required YYYY-MM-DD format), and JSON strings carry no type information.
rules.check: Look for decoders that try to parse a JSON string as a date or number and then retype it (for example as `ClaimValueTypes.DateTime`) or rewrite its value.

rules.statement: When encoding a value whose declared type is a date (for example `ClaimValueTypes.DateTime`), parse it with `DateCoercion.TryParseDateTimeOffset`, and if parsing fails, including for an instant that can't be represented, emit the original string unchanged rather than a clamped or machine-local guess.
rules.why: Encoding should follow the producer's declared type and must never write a wrong instant.
rules.check: Look for date-typed encoding paths that parse with something other than `DateCoercion`, or that replace an unparseable value with a default, clamped or local-time value.
